Given any change, then it is kept in the asset history.
Given the M01 simple asset register, then its data moves here and M01 uses this model.

title: Asset manager assigns and scans assets
story: As an asset manager, I want to assign assets and scan their tags, so that check-in and check-out are quick.
acceptance: Given an asset, then it can be assigned to a person, location or department, and checked in or out.
Given a barcode or QR tag, then the mobile app (M04) scan opens the asset.
Given M01 onboarding or exit, then assets are issued or returned through this flow.

title: Finance tracks warranty, AMC, lease and depreciation
story: As a finance user, I want warranties, AMCs, leases and depreciation tracked, so that renewals and books are right.
acceptance: Given warranty, AMC or lease end dates, then reminders go before expiry.
Given depreciation, then straight line and written-down value methods are available.
Given a period, then a depreciation report can be exported.

title: IT admin enrols devices with osquery
story: As an IT admin, I want devices found automatically, so that the inventory is always current.
acceptance: Given the company enrolment key, then osquery enrols through our TLS enrol, config and logger endpoints; no own agent code runs on devices.
Given each device, then it has its own revocable key, TLS uses our pinned certificate, and the company secret can be rotated.
Given collected data, then it is inventory only: no browsing history, no files, no personal data.

title: Discovery never runs remote actions
story: As a company IT admin, I want YukthiX unable to control our devices, so that a YukthiX breach cannot reach them.
acceptance: Given the agent, then it runs only our fixed read-only query pack.
Given any request for remote commands, scripts or ad-hoc live queries, then the API has no way to send them.
Given remote control needs, then the docs point to the company's own MDM.

title: IT admin downloads signed installers
story: As an IT admin, I want code-signed installers for Windows and macOS, so that devices trust them.
acceptance: Given Windows and macOS installers, then they are code-signed and carry the company enrolment settings.
Given Linux, then a package and a script are provided.
Given a new installer version, then devices on the old version are listed for update.

title: Asset manager tracks software licences
story: As an asset manager, I want licence entitlements against installations, so that we stay compliant.
acceptance: Given a licence, then entitlements are compared with discovered installations.
Given more installs than entitlements, then a compliance alert is raised.
Given a renewal date, then reminders go before it.

title: IT admin imports devices from MDM and CSV
story: As an IT admin, I want devices from Intune, Jamf, Google Workspace or CSV, so that we start with a full list.
acceptance: Given an Intune, Jamf or Google Workspace connection, then devices import and update on a schedule.
Given a CSV file, then a preview shows errors before import.
Given the same device from two sources, then they are merged by serial number.

title: IT admin finds office devices with a read-only probe
story: As an IT admin, I want an office probe to find printers and network devices, so that unmanaged devices are in the list.
acceptance: Given the office probe, then it uses read-only SNMP and ARP only; nmap is not used or bundled.
Given found devices, then they appear as "discovered" until the admin confirms them as assets.
Given the probe, then it is set up with a company key and can be switched off at any time.

title: Configuration management (CMDB)
IT admin keeps configuration items and their relations
story: As an IT admin, I want CIs with relations and a map, so that I see what depends on what.
acceptance: Given CI types, then each has custom attributes.
Given relations (runs on, depends on, connected to), then a visual dependency map is shown.
Given a CI, then its history and baselines are kept.

title: Agent sees the impact of an incident or change
story: As a change manager, I want impact analysis from the CMDB, so that I know what a change may break.
acceptance: Given an incident or change on a CI, then the CIs and services that depend on it are listed.
Given a change, then affected CI owners can be added as approvers.
Given impact analysis, then it shows the open incidents on the dependent CIs.

title: Vendors, contracts and procurement
Asset manager keeps vendors and contracts
story: As an asset manager, I want vendors and contracts with renewal dates, so that nothing expires by surprise.
acceptance: Given a contract, then it has vendor, value, SLA and renewal date.
Given a renewal date, then reminders go before it.
Given a vendor SLA, then it is used as an underpinning contract on tickets.

title: Requester asks to buy an asset and it is received into stock
story: As an asset manager, I want purchase requests, orders and receiving, so that new assets enter the register correctly.
acceptance: Given a purchase request, then it follows approvals and becomes a purchase order to a vendor.
Given goods received, then assets are created "in stock" with the PO reference.
Given a part delivery, then only the received quantity is added to stock and the order stays open.

title: Monitoring and event management
Monitoring alerts create and close incidents
story: As an on-call engineer, I want alerts from monitoring tools to become incidents, so that nothing is missed.
acceptance: Given webhooks from Prometheus / Grafana, Datadog, Azure Monitor, CloudWatch or uptime tools, then alerts are received and checked.
Given repeated or related alerts, then they are de-duplicated and grouped into one incident.
Given a recovery alert, then the incident closes automatically with a note.

title: On-call and escalation
Team lead sets on-call schedules and rotations
story: As a team lead, I want on-call rotations, so that someone is always responsible.
acceptance: Given a schedule, then rotations, hand-over times and overrides can be set.
Given now, then the console shows who is on call for each team.
Given a holiday or leave, then an override can hand the shift to a colleague.

title: On-call engineer is paged and acknowledges
story: As an on-call engineer, I want to be paged by SMS, call or push, so that I wake up for real problems.
acceptance: Given an urgent incident, then the on-call person is paged by SMS, call or push through P04.
Given no acknowledgement in the set time, then the escalation policy pages the next level.
Given acknowledgement, then the time is recorded for MTTA.

title: Status pages for companies
Company publishes its own status pages
story: As a company IT lead, I want public and private status pages, so that our users see service health.
acceptance: Given components, then the company can publish public or private (signed-in) status pages using the same engine as the YukthiX status page (YX-GRO-09).
Given an incident, then updates post to the page and subscribers are notified.
Given subscribers, then sign-up uses double opt-in and one-click unsubscribe.

title: Major incident
Lead declares a major incident with a war-room
story: As an incident manager, I want to declare a major incident, so that the right people work together at once.
acceptance: Given an incident, when the manager declares it major, then a war-room (bridge) is opened and key people are paged.
Given stakeholder updates, then reminders go on the set schedule until resolved.
Given the incident, then all linked tickets show a banner.

title: Team writes a post-incident review
story: As an incident manager, I want a review after a major incident, so that we prevent it next time.
acceptance: Given a resolved major incident, then a review task is created with timeline, cause, fix and actions.
Given actions, then each has an owner and a due date and can become a problem record.
Given the review, then it can be shared with customers as a post-incident summary.

title: AI assistance
AI suggests category, routing and duplicates
story: As a team lead, I want AI to categorise and route new tickets, so that agents start work sooner.
acceptance: Given a new ticket, then AI suggests category, priority and queue with a confidence level.
Given low confidence, then the ticket goes to manual triage.
Given a likely duplicate, then the agent is shown the matching ticket.

title: AI suggests replies, articles and summaries
story: As an agent, I want suggested replies, article links and a summary, so that I answer faster.
acceptance: Given a ticket, then AI offers a draft reply and related articles; the agent must review before sending.
Given a long ticket, then a short summary is shown.
Given sentiment or urgency signals, then the ticket is flagged.
Given sensitive categories, then AI uses only data the agent may already see (YX-HD-03).

title: Virtual agent answers from the knowledge base
story: As an employee, I want a virtual agent that answers from articles and policies, so that I get help at any time.
acceptance: Given a question, then the virtual agent answers from published articles and policies with links.
Given it cannot answer, then it raises a ticket with the conversation.
Given an answer that solves it, then it counts as deflected (YX-HD-04).

title: Projects and tasks
IT lead runs simple projects and tasks
story: As an IT lead, I want simple projects and tasks for work that is not a ticket, so that all IT work is in one place.
acceptance: Given a project, then it has tasks with owners, due dates and status.
Given a company with M12, then projects link to it instead of duplicating.
Given a ticket that turns into larger work, then it can be linked to a project task.

title: Facilities booking and visitors
Employee books a room or desk
story: As an employee, I want to book a room or desk, so that I have a place to work or meet.
acceptance: Given rooms and desks per location, then employees can book free slots.
Given a clash, then the second booking is refused.
Given a no-show, then the booking is released after the set time.

title: Employee requests a visitor pass or maintenance
story: As an employee, I want to request a visitor pass or a repair, so that the facilities team acts.
acceptance: Given a visitor request, then the facilities desk gets it with visitor name and time.
Given a maintenance request, then it becomes a facilities ticket with location.
Given a visitor pass, then the host is told when the visitor arrives.

title: Importers, sandbox and integrations
Desk admin imports from other help desks
story: As a desk admin, I want to import tickets, articles and assets from Zoho Desk, Freshservice, Jira SM or CSV, so that switching is easy.
acceptance: Given a source, then a dry run shows counts and errors before import.
Given an import, then old ids are kept as references and history is preserved.
Given a failed import, then it can be rolled back.

title: Desk admin tests configuration in a sandbox
story: As a desk admin, I want to try rule and form changes in a sandbox, so that live work is not broken.
acceptance: Given a P15 sandbox, then desk settings can be copied and changed there.
Given tested changes, then they can be promoted to live with an audit entry.
Given a sandbox, then no email, SMS or WhatsApp reaches real requesters from it.

title: Desk admin connects integrations from the marketplace
story: As a desk admin, I want ready integrations (Teams, Slack, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Intune, Jamf, Jira / GitHub, monitoring), so that we connect tools in minutes.
acceptance: Given the P23 marketplace, then each integration shows what data moves and can be switched on by an admin.
Given an integration, then its secrets are stored encrypted and its errors show on the Jobs & errors page.
Given an integration switched off, then it stops at once and its stored secrets are deleted.
